_doc.about: OpenPGP behavior every client must match: web (shared/src/pgp, TypeScript, openpgp.js) and Android :core (Kotlin). Contract: docs/pgp-contract.md. Strings use CRLF where messages do. Made by shared/src/pgp/make-fixtures.ts.
_doc.keys: Test people only: each test run makes its own key pairs for them (Curve25519, EdDSA legacy primary + ECDH Curve25519 subkey, v4, created 2026-01-01, unprotected), so this file holds no private key. Web: shared/src/pgp/test-fixtures.ts; Android: FixtureMessages.kt.
_doc.seal: seal(secret, plaintext, iv) == sealed and unseal(secret, sealed) == plaintext. Key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=secret, salt=empty, info=UTF-8 'inbox.hafa.cc/pgp-seal/v1', 32 bytes); AES-256-GCM, no AAD; sealed = base64(0x01 || iv(12) || ciphertext || tag(16)). unsealFailures must throw.
_doc.phraseWords: wordsFromBytes(bytes, 8): big-endian 16-bit numbers, skip ≥ 62208, word = list[n % 7776] (shared/wordlists/eff_large_wordlist.txt, line n+1).
_doc.parsePhrase: parsePhrase(input): lower-case, split on whitespace (not hyphens), unknown = indexes not in the list, normalized = words joined by one space when 8 known words, else null.
_doc.recovery: recoverySecret(phrase, salt, kdf) == secretHex: Argon2id v0x13, password = UTF-8 of the normalized phrase, 32-byte output. unsealWithPhrase(phrase, sealed) == plaintext; also with phraseTyped.
_doc.wkd: wkdHash(local) and wkdUrls(address): z-base-32 of SHA-1 of the local part with A-Z lower-cased; the l= parameter is the local part as given, percent-encoded.
_doc.autocrypt: build: autocryptHeaderValue(address, publicKey) == value (key data in 64-character pieces joined by spaces); publicKey is a test public key whose private key was thrown away. The key data is the key re-serialized, so packets a keyring adds (a trust packet) are left out. parse: parseAutocrypt(value) → null, or addr, preferEncrypt and keydata (base64 of the bytes). for: autocryptFor(values, from) → addr or null.
_doc.decision: encryptionDecision(from, recipients, keys) where keys maps each address in withKeys to a key and the rest to null.
_doc.protect: protectedParts(mime) == { outerHeaders, inner }; assemblePgpMime(outerHeaders, placeholder, boundary) == assembled. mime is buildMime(composeInput) from compose-fixtures' rules (boundary token fixture1). Also: decrypting encryptMime(mime, …) gives back inner byte for byte.
_doc.decrypt: Build the message with this run's keys, signing at 2026-01-02: encrypt pgp.data (binary, or text when format is text) to pgp.to's keys, signed by each of pgp.signers in order; for {{signature}} in data, first put the armored detached binary signature by pgp.signature.by over the UTF-8 of pgp.signature.over. Armored blocks go in with CRLF line breaks and none at the end. In raw, {{pgp}} is that armored message, {{pgp:qp}} the same with each = written =3D, and {{pgp:base64}} the base64 (76-character lines, CRLF) of 'Hi', the fewest '!' that make the UTF-8 byte count 2 mod 3, CRLF CRLF and the armored message. A case with encryptMime instead of raw is encryptMime(mime, to's public keys, signer's private key, boundary). The message is the UTF-8 of the result. Then decryptMessage(message, { decryptionKeys: [keys[k].privateKey], verificationKeys: [keys[k].publicKey…] }). expect: kind, signature status, protectedHeaders (null or the map), mismatchedHeaders, type of the decrypted entity, and text = the decoded first text/plain part. Or error = PgpError code; otherwise also encryptionKind(parseMime(message)) == kind. PGP/MIME is a multipart/encrypted (protocol application/pgp-encrypted) at the root or as a direct child of the root. Signature: the first signature whose key id is one of the verification keys' (primary or subkey) decides valid/invalid; unknown-key (with the first signature's key id) when none is. protectedHeaders: from, reply-to, to and cc come from inside only when the signature is valid and its key has a user id whose address equals the inner From's single address (case-insensitive); otherwise each present inside is replaced by the outer header's decoded value (removed when the outer message has none), and listed in mismatchedHeaders (in the order from, reply-to, to, cc) when the two differ after collapsing whitespace runs to one space and trimming.
_doc.headerDecode: decodeHeaderValue(value) == expect: RFC 2047 encoded words decoded (whitespace between two adjacent encoded words dropped); a word that fails to decode (bad base64) stays exactly as written.

From: Bob Test <bob@example.com>
To: Alice Test <test@hafa.cc>
Subject: ...
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: multipart/encrypted; protocol="application/pgp-encrypted";
 boundary="=_fx_enc"

This is an OpenPGP/MIME encrypted message (RFC 4880 and 3156)
--=_fx_enc
Content-Type: application/pgp-encrypted
Content-Description: PGP/MIME version identification

Version: 1

--=_fx_enc
Content-Type: application/octet-stream; name="encrypted.asc"
Content-Description: OpenPGP encrypted message
Content-Disposition: inline; filename="encrypted.asc"

{{pgp}}
--=_fx_enc--

pgp.data:
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64

Tm8gcGFkZGluZzogY2Fmw6kh
